title: The nickname 'Rat' and the Magnolia Band
summary: Dawson explains how passing the hat got him called Rat, names the Magnolia Band players, and recalls Bechet and bands' habit of changing men.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Sidney Bechet: the man, the horn, the legend

blocks.x: Who were they? Yeah, Alphonse Peek Good and Javala. Where was it? That was down at Miller Phillips. I mean at Hunts and Nagels.
And what did they call you? They called me a rat.

Well, I'll tell you why, you know. We used to have to pass the hat around, you see. Mm-hmm. Pick up tips. And I'd run around with the hat, you know, and come back. And I was so fast, you know, that's when they started to call me a rat. And they started to call me a rat then. From that on, all the musicians, practically every one of them, most of them. Old ones, all of them knowed me about rats.
And who was the clarinet by that? You said it was Piku then, huh?
Alphonse Peek Good, yeah. He played with the... Was there another one there? No.
Any other clarinet player of them?
No. No, just Peek Good and Eddie Atkins was playing trombone, you know, I think. That's been a long time. Eddie Atkins and Piku. That was the Magnolia Band.
Mm-hmm. I thought you said there was a little dog fellow there on clarinet at one time.

Well, he did have me meet you. He's dead now. I'm trying to think his name off. Y'all know him good, too. He died up in a parish somewhere up in France. You mean Sidney Bichet? Sidney Bichet. Sidney Bichet.
And you said he was about to bash tail on there earlier.

Yes, indeed. He was playing with... You see them bands, that time, you know, they'd have a little fallin' out with a fallin' like that. They'd get another fallin', you know. They'd have a regular man. They all do the same thing. They'd have a regular man and if they have some kind of a little grievance with that man, then when you look around, he either quits or they're five and they'd get another fallin' and he'd stay with them a while and then... That's the way it was. You couldn't just keep... study men all the time. They used to have a little... just a misunderstanding between, you know. And if you're gettin' bad with the leader, well then you know what the consequence is. He'd serve to make it so miserable for you that you'd have to quit before he'd fire.
